demo.title: From scattered sources to selected AI context
transcript: Begin by saving a useful webpage or converting documents and scans into local Markdown.
Search the SourceShelf Library, choose the sources that matter, and arrange them into an ordered saved pack.
Export the pack as portable context or authorize an immutable, read-only snapshot for a compatible AI client.
Use Refresh & Compare later to review changes, and revoke Local AI Access whenever the share is no longer needed.

sections.heading: Bring scattered knowledge together
paragraphs: Useful information rarely lives in one place. It is spread across reports, PDFs, slide decks, spreadsheets, scanned pages, notes, and browser tabs. SourceShelf brings those materials into a searchable local Library while preserving where each source came from.

Save a useful article from Safari, convert a folder of project documents, or use local OCR on a scanned PDF. SourceShelf turns the result into structured Markdown that remains accessible outside the app.

links.label: See how local PDF conversion works
Explore Safari webpage capture

sections.heading: Create focused packs for real work
paragraphs: Build an ordered knowledge pack for a research project, course, client, investigation, or recurring task. Include only the sources that matter and arrange them in the order that makes sense.
A focused pack gives a compatible AI assistant relevant material without exposing the rest of your Library or repeatedly attaching the same files.

links.label: Create focused AI reference packs
Build a durable local research archive

sections.heading: Use the AI you choose
paragraphs: SourceShelf is not another AI chatbot and does not lock your knowledge to one model. A compatible AI client on your Mac can connect to a saved pack through read-only Model Context Protocol access.
The client may use a model running locally on your Mac or a cloud-backed model. SourceShelf itself does not upload the pack or call an AI service.

links.label: Understand read-only MCP knowledge access

sections.heading: Only the pack you approve
paragraphs: Each Local AI authorization creates an immutable snapshot containing only the saved pack you selected. AI clients can search that snapshot and read bounded passages, but they cannot change your sources or browse arbitrary files.
Original file paths, security bookmarks, output-folder locations, and unselected Library items are not included. Stop sharing the pack at any time to invalidate the connection.

sections.heading: Open files, not a closed vault
paragraphs: SourceShelf's generated sources are ordinary Markdown files. Open them in your preferred editor, make changes, and return to SourceShelf when you are ready.
Refresh & Compare shows what was added, changed, removed, or left unchanged before you update an export or shared AI snapshot.

faq.question: Does SourceShelf include an AI model?
faq.answer: No. SourceShelf prepares and organizes knowledge for compatible AI applications. You remain free to choose the local or cloud-backed model you use.

faq.question: Does SourceShelf upload my documents?
faq.answer: No. SourceShelf performs its own capture, conversion, OCR, organization, and export work locally on your Mac.

faq.question: Can a smaller local model use a SourceShelf pack?
faq.answer: Yes, when the model is used through a compatible AI client. SourceShelf provides focused search results and bounded source passages so the client does not need to load every document at once.

faq.question: Can an AI client edit or delete my sources?
faq.answer: No. SourceShelf's MCP access is read-only and limited to the immutable snapshot of the pack you authorize.

closing.heading: Build a private knowledge base from the sources you trust
closing.description: Keep your knowledge local, portable, and deliberately scoped for the AI workflow you choose.

sections.heading: Text PDFs and scanned PDFs
paragraphs: SourceShelf handles PDFs that already contain selectable text and image-only PDFs that require OCR. When no usable text is available, it uses Apple's local document-recognition technology on your Mac.
The document does not need to be sent to an online converter or external OCR service.

sections.heading: Useful structure, not just a text dump
paragraphs: SourceShelf builds a semantic representation of the document before rendering Markdown. Where the source allows it, the result retains useful elements such as headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, code, quotations, captions, images, and page boundaries.
Complex layouts and imperfect scans can still require correction, but the result is designed to be readable, inspectable, and portable.

sections.heading: Your Markdown remains yours
paragraphs: Generated Markdown is written to the output folder you choose. Open it in your preferred Markdown editor, reveal it in Finder, or use it with other tools.
SourceShelf detects external edits and regenerates its local semantic cache without overwriting the changes you made.

faq.question: Does PDF conversion require an internet connection?
faq.answer: No. SourceShelf performs PDF extraction and OCR locally.

faq.question: Can it convert scanned PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes. SourceShelf can use local Apple OCR when a PDF has no selectable text.

faq.question: Will every complex layout be reproduced perfectly?
faq.answer: No. OCR and document reconstruction can require correction, particularly with low-quality scans or complex multi-column layouts. SourceShelf preserves useful structure where extraction allows it.

faq.question: Can I edit the Markdown afterward?

sections.heading: Help smaller models find the right material
paragraphs: A local model often has less available context than a large hosted model. Instead of handing it every file in a project, SourceShelf lets you create a focused pack containing only the sources relevant to the task.

Compatible clients can search the pack and request bounded passages, helping the model use its available context on the material that matters. This can help, but it does not guarantee a better or more accurate answer.

sections.heading: One source collection, several workflows
paragraphs: Use an AI Reference Pack ZIP for project workspaces and AI chats, a Markdown Context Pack for portable one-file context, an llms.txt Collection Folder for an open local collection, or an OKF bundle for standards-based catalogs and agents.

sections.heading: Advanced formats
items: AI Reference Pack ZIP: a structured bundle for project workspaces and AI-assisted tasks.
Markdown Context Pack: one portable Markdown file containing the selected source material.
llms.txt Collection Folder: an open local collection organized around llms.txt conventions.
OKF bundle: a standards-based catalog and source package for compatible tools and agents.

sections.heading: Retrieval-ready without model lock-in
paragraphs: AI Reference Packs can include structure-aware chunks with stable IDs, heading ancestry, provenance, hashes, and asset references.
SourceShelf does not create proprietary indexes or model-specific embeddings. The original Markdown remains usable with other tools and future workflows.

sections.heading: Export a pack or connect it directly
paragraphs: Export when you need a portable artifact. Use Local AI Access when a compatible client should search and read a saved pack directly.

Local AI Access creates a read-only snapshot rather than exposing live original files. SourceShelf refreshes a shared snapshot only when a fresh Trust & Safety result is available and the update is allowed.

links.label: Learn how pack-scoped MCP access works

sections.heading: Know when your context changed
paragraphs: After an export, Refresh & Compare records a local baseline and reports new, changed, missing, unchanged, and removed sources along with ordering changes.
This makes it easier to understand whether an AI reference pack still represents the current state of your research.

faq.question: Does SourceShelf run a local AI model?
faq.answer: No. It prepares and serves selected source material to compatible AI clients. You choose the model and client.

faq.question: Does SourceShelf create embeddings?
faq.answer: No. It can create structured retrieval chunks, but it does not bundle model-specific embeddings.

faq.question: What is the difference between export and Local AI Access?
faq.answer: An export creates a portable file or folder. Local AI Access lets a compatible client search and read an authorized saved-pack snapshot on your Mac.

faq.question: Can an AI client see the rest of my Library?
faq.answer: No. The client receives access only to the snapshot of the saved pack you explicitly authorize.

faq.question: Does SourceShelf replace a reference manager?
faq.answer: SourceShelf focuses on capturing, converting, organizing, and packaging source content. It does not currently provide formal citation-style or bibliography management.

faq.question: Where are generated sources stored?
faq.answer: They are written to the local output folder selected by the user.

faq.question: Can I open SourceShelf Markdown in another app?
faq.answer: Yes. Generated sources are normal Markdown files and open in the editor configured on your Mac.

faq.question: Does SourceShelf automatically delete old research?
faq.answer: No. Library sources remain until the user explicitly removes them.

sections.heading: MCP without the jargon
paragraphs: A compatible AI application sometimes needs a way to request information from another application. Model Context Protocol provides that connection.
With SourceShelf, you choose a saved pack and authorize it for Local AI Access. The AI client can then ask SourceShelf to find relevant passages and read approved text resources from that pack.

sections.heading: A pack boundary you can understand
paragraphs: SourceShelf does not expose the live Library or give the client a general filesystem tool. It creates an immutable copy of the selected pack under a random authorization identifier.

The snapshot contains copied Markdown, referenced local images, a catalog, checksums, and an allowlist. It excludes original paths, output-folder paths, security bookmarks, and every Library source outside the pack.

sections.heading: Search first, read only what is needed
paragraphs: A compatible client first asks SourceShelf to find relevant passages inside the authorized pack. It can then read an approved text source in bounded pages rather than loading every document at once.

sections.heading: Advanced MCP details
sections.summary: See the exact read-only tools and connection boundary
items: search_pack finds relevant structure-aware passages inside the authorized pack.
read_pack_resource reads an allowlisted text source in bounded pages.
The helper provides no prompts, subscriptions, write tools, arbitrary paths, remote fetching, or network listener.
The compatible AI client launches the helper locally and SourceShelf reloads authorization information for every request.

sections.heading: No write access and no network server
paragraphs: The SourceShelf MCP helper cannot edit sources, delete files, fetch remote content, browse arbitrary paths, or listen for network connections. It communicates locally through a command launched by the compatible AI client.
Stopping a share or disabling MCP invalidates the copied configuration immediately.

sections.heading: Local or cloud-backed models remain your choice
paragraphs: MCP connects the desktop AI client to SourceShelf. The client may use a model running on the Mac or a cloud-backed model.
SourceShelf controls the local knowledge connection but does not control the privacy policy or data handling of the third-party AI client you choose.

faq.question: What does MCP mean?
faq.answer: Model Context Protocol is a standard way for compatible applications to request context and tools from another application. SourceShelf uses it for local, read-only access to an authorized knowledge pack.

faq.question: Does MCP give an AI access to my whole Mac?
faq.answer: No. SourceShelf exposes only the immutable snapshot of the saved pack you authorize.

faq.question: Can the AI change my documents?
faq.answer: No. SourceShelf provides no MCP write, delete, or arbitrary-file tools.

faq.question: Can a cloud-backed AI client use the connection?
faq.answer: Potentially, when its desktop application supports the required local MCP connection. The third-party client's own privacy and data-handling terms still apply.

faq.question: How do I revoke access?
faq.answer: Stop the individual pack share or disable Local AI Access in SourceShelf. The helper reloads authorization information for every request, so revoked access stops working immediately.
